title: All Prime members
context: The growth team is preparing a Prime-exclusive promotion.
task: List first_name, last_name and country for every customer who is a Prime member.
answer: SELECT first_name, last_name, country FROM customers WHERE prime_member = 1;

title: Product catalogue
context: Merchandising wants a plain list of what's for sale.
task: Return name, category and price for every product.
answer: SELECT name, category, price FROM products;

title: Countries we ship to
context: Legal needs the list of countries with at least one customer.
task: Return each distinct country from customers.
answer: SELECT DISTINCT country FROM customers;

title: Product categories
context: The nav bar needs one entry per category.
task: Return the distinct category values from products.
answer: SELECT DISTINCT category FROM products;

title: Products in stock
context: Merchandising wants a quick view of what's currently sellable.
task: Return name and price where stock is greater than 50, ordered by price descending.
answer: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE stock > 50 ORDER BY price DESC;

title: Out of stock
context: Ops wants the list of products that can't be sold right now.
task: Return product_id and name for products with stock = 0.
answer: SELECT product_id, name FROM products WHERE stock = 0;

title: Big-ticket orders
context: Fraud review looks at high-value orders first.
task: Return order_id, customer_id and total_amount for orders above 300.
answer: SELECT order_id, customer_id, total_amount FROM orders WHERE total_amount > 300;

title: Cancelled orders
context: Support wants to follow up on cancellations.
task: Return order_id and order_date for orders with status 'cancelled'.
answer: SELECT order_id, order_date FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled';

title: Indian Prime members
context: A regional Prime Day campaign is launching in India.
task: Return first_name and last_name of customers from India who are Prime members.
answer: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM customers WHERE country = 'India' AND prime_member = 1;

title: Electronics and Kitchen
context: The home tech landing page shows two categories.
task: Return name and category for products in the 'Electronics' or 'Kitchen' categories.
answer: SELECT name, category FROM products WHERE category IN ('Electronics','Kitchen');

title: Everything but delivered
context: Ops wants to see every order that is still open or went wrong.
task: Return order_id and status for orders whose status is not 'delivered'.
answer: SELECT order_id, status FROM orders WHERE status <> 'delivered';

title: Mid-range products
context: A 'gifts under 100' page needs items priced 25 to 100.
task: Return name and price for products priced between 25 and 100 inclusive.
answer: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 25 AND 100;

title: Q1 2024 orders
context: Finance is closing the first quarter.
task: Return order_id and order_date for orders placed from 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.
hint: Dates are ISO text, so BETWEEN works.
answer: SELECT order_id, order_date FROM orders WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2024-01-01' AND '2024-03-31';

title: Kindle and Fire devices
context: The devices team tracks their own products.
task: Return name for products whose name starts with 'Kindle' or 'Fire'.
answer: SELECT name FROM products WHERE name LIKE 'Kindle%' OR name LIKE 'Fire%';

title: Names containing 'an'
context: Support is searching for a customer they half-remember.
task: Return first_name and last_name of customers whose first_name contains 'an'.
answer: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM customers WHERE first_name LIKE '%an%';

title: Missing emails
context: A data-quality audit found some customers can't be contacted.
task: Return customer_id, first_name and last_name for customers with no email.
answer: SELECT customer_id, first_name, last_name FROM customers WHERE email IS NULL;

title: Corporate employees
context: HR needs the staff not attached to any warehouse.
task: Return first_name, last_name and department for employees with no warehouse_id.
answer: SELECT first_name, last_name, department FROM employees WHERE warehouse_id IS NULL;

title: Newest customers first
context: Onboarding wants to see the most recent signups.
task: Return first_name, last_name and signup_date sorted by signup_date descending.
answer: SELECT first_name, last_name, signup_date FROM customers ORDER BY signup_date DESC;

title: Employees by department then salary
context: HR is preparing the pay review sheet.
task: Return first_name, department and salary sorted by department ascending, then salary descending.
answer: SELECT first_name, department, salary FROM employees ORDER BY department, salary DESC;

title: Top 5 priciest products
context: The luxury carousel shows five items.
task: Return name and price for the 5 most expensive products.
answer: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 5;

title: Three biggest orders
context: Leadership wants the largest orders of the period.
task: Return order_id and total_amount for the 3 largest orders by total_amount.
answer: SELECT order_id, total_amount FROM orders ORDER BY total_amount DESC LIMIT 3;

title: Stock value per product
context: Finance values inventory at list price.
task: Return name and stock_value = price * stock for every product, rounded to 2 decimals.
answer: SELECT name, ROUND(price * stock, 2) AS stock_value FROM products;

title: Line totals
context: The invoice shows a total per line item.
task: Return item_id and line_total = quantity * unit_price for every order item.
answer: SELECT item_id, quantity * unit_price AS line_total FROM order_items;

title: Full names
context: The CRM export wants one name column.
task: Return full_name = first_name, a space, last_name for every customer.
answer: SELECT first_name || ' ' || last_name AS full_name FROM customers;

title: Uppercase categories
context: Category labels are shown in caps on the storefront.
task: Return product name and category in upper case as category_upper.
answer: SELECT name, UPPER(category) AS category_upper FROM products;

title: How many Prime members?
context: The quarterly deck needs a Prime headline number.
task: Return prime_count = number of customers with prime_member = 1.
answer: SELECT COUNT(*) AS prime_count FROM customers WHERE prime_member = 1;

title: Customers who ordered
context: Marketing wants active customers, not order volume.
task: Return active_customers = number of distinct customer_id values in orders.
answer: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS active_customers FROM orders;

title: Delivered revenue
context: Finance recognises revenue only on delivered orders.
task: Return revenue = sum of total_amount for delivered orders, rounded to 2 decimals.
answer: SELECT ROUND(SUM(total_amount), 2) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE status = 'delivered';

title: Average order value
context: AOV is a key metric on the dashboard.
task: Return aov = average total_amount across all orders, rounded to 2 decimals.
answer: SELECT ROUND(AVG(total_amount), 2) AS aov FROM orders;

title: Salary range
context: HR is benchmarking pay bands.
task: Return min_salary and max_salary across all employees.
hint: MIN and MAX in one query.
answer: SELECT MIN(salary) AS min_salary, MAX(salary) AS max_salary FROM employees;

title: Customers per country
context: The map widget needs counts by country.
task: Return country and customer_count for each country.
answer: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY country;

title: Orders by status
context: Ops tracks the order pipeline.
task: Return status and order_count for each status.
answer: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY status;

title: Average price per category
context: Pricing wants to compare categories.
task: Return category and avg_price (rounded to 2 decimals) for each category.
answer: SELECT category, ROUND(AVG(price), 2) AS avg_price FROM products GROUP BY category;

title: Employee warehouse assignment
context: Fulfillment Ops is reviewing where each warehouse employee sits.
task: Return first_name, last_name and warehouse location for employees assigned to a warehouse.
hint: INNER JOIN drops NULL warehouse_id rows for free.
answer: SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, w.location FROM employees e JOIN warehouses w ON e.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id;
